head: 79a09f778c4dfa1f79f1fd6320bec1dd9bac9146
adjudication_item: b84 item (d): the L4 build/link atlas row for `openssh` recorded an artefact its own recipe built, not the binary the OpenSSH closure analyses

recipe_change.mechanism: _RECIPE_OVERRIDES['openssh'] (the table seam the kmod/openvpn/isync overrides already use); no code special-cases openssh
unchanged: specimen and variant rows (byte-identical to the committed ones)
recipe_change.argument: the row now expresses the closure's build intent: the closure's five configure flags, the candidate lib directory on the run path through LDFLAGS (the released Linux configure leaves rpath_opt empty), and a full make rather than `make ssh`. {root}/.l7-install is the convention the irssi recipe already uses; {prefix} remains the admitted subject's OpenSSL prefix, so the identical-build-intent rule is preserved.

venue.note: the court was re-created before this measurement because the 37h-old container had drifted to memory.swap.max=max, which is not the documented venue (swap pinned to the memory cap). Records under the documented venue are byte-identical to the committed ones, so the only rows this measurement rewrites are the two `openssh` rows plus the durable `reused_from_candidate_identity` marker on the reused rows.

rows_changed.detail: the 612 reused rows carry the marker because the committed atlas was measured against candidate install libcrypto 6d401e06…, not the current 53df5493…; that is the tool's designed durable provenance, not a re-measurement of those families

digest_identity.exact_remaining_difference: the absolute build root compiled into the artefact. Two things embed it: (1) the configure-derived path macros (-DSSH_SYSCONFDIR etc. from --prefix/--sysconfdir), so `ssh` carries its default config/known-hosts paths; (2) DWARF: the compile directory and line-table file names (OpenSSH's default CFLAGS carry -g). The atlas builds at {scratch}/openssh/candidate/src/openssh-9.9p1 with prefix {root}/.l7-install; the closure builds at /work/court/tmp/openssh-closure/client-b84/openssh-9.9p1 with prefix /work/court/tmp/openssh-closure/client-b84/install. Neither path is expressible by a data-driven recipe (the atlas substitutes only {prefix}/{root}/{aux}/{repo}), and the closure path carries a per-run role tag. Byte-identity would require hardcoding a tag-specific closure path in the recipe, which is exactly the special-casing this batch was asked to avoid.

determinism_evidence.method: the row's own build was reconstructed at its exact recorded path and argv (court/freeze-b84/review13/build-atlas-row.sh), from the same pinned tarball, in the same image

comparison_with_closure_binary.debug_line_str_bytes: 0xb57 (atlas) vs 0xb43 (closure): the only structural difference, 20 bytes
comparison_with_closure_binary.path_strings: 15 in each binary; identical after normalising each build root and install prefix
comparison_with_closure_binary.conclusion: same build intent, same toolchain, same venue, same source, same linked sonames and runpath; the sole difference is the embedded absolute build root

self_test.result: ok (guard refusal, acquire-failure accounting, zero findings on the committed atlas, and every seeded mutation caught)

artifact_matches_this_build_conclusion.reason: the row's digest is 45da459f… and the analysed binary's is 2eb4b8b3…, so the predicate is still false and the closure would still append the 'produced against a different candidate install' note. Comparing the atlas row digest with the receipt's artifact_identity.sha256 (evidence/closure-ssh-b84b.json, sha256 2ea7613c…, artifact_identity.sha256 2eb4b8b3…) shows the same inequality without re-running a closure.
artifact_matches_this_build_conclusion.what_the_change_does_fix: the second half of the same defect: the row's recorded_candidate_install moves from 6d401e06… to 53df5493…, the freeze-proven install, so `recorded_install_matches_freeze_install` becomes true and the row's source/specimen identity is unchanged.
what_a_true_binding_now_requires: either a closure rebuilt at a path the atlas can express (a new S and a new artefact identity — out of scope for this batch), or

a build-intent binding rather than a byte-equality binding: the per-artefact rebind path (evidence/ssh-artifact-ledger-b84-rebind.json, sha256 33093d6ea0b59822af0427abd13238d309f78e7f8632e4a28485a4cb493c88e1, artifact_matches_this_build true) joins the closure artefact to the freeze digest on (recipe_id, source_sha256, source_root_hash, candidate install), and this row now agrees with it on every one of those fields

residuals: the `openssh-server` (sshd) row still builds `make -j8 ssh sshd sshd-session ssh-keygen` with the atlas's own configure flags; its candidate digest is dccccf07… while the closure's analysed sshd is cdf61204…. Item (d) named only `openssh`, so this is left for the adjudicator to schedule (the same per-artefact rebind receipt covers it).

FREEZE-b84.json (court/, untracked) still records the previous atlas identity (atlas_sha256 15f5a222…, body_hash 927ecfdd…) in its ledger_binding; it must be re-derived against atlas_sha256 f4654ec3… / body_hash 556e2b4b… before any fresh closure receipt cites it.
no closure was re-run (deliberately): the conclusion above is drawn from the receipt's recorded artifact_identity.sha256, not from a new 45-minute run.
not_run: OpenSSH closure re-run (L7 replay) against the new atlas row
